clue.text: Distributed on all pitches, but not uniform

indicators.note: things distributed are spread about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: all twelve letters of the phrase are the fodder

explanation.surface: Players spread across every pitch, yet none wearing team kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like sports kit; the definition points to detectives who work out of police uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers in plain clothes are on duty without wearing the regulation outfit.

clue.text: Pull young lady up: a dawdler!

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to drag is to pull
gal is informal for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone urges a slow girl to get a move on.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is a person who falls behind, a slowcoach or straggler.

clue.text: Green endpiece in Rex's jumble

indicators.note: a jumble is a disordered heap, so the preceding letters are mixed up

blocks.note: all thirteen letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A green fragment turns up among the clutter belonging to someone called Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' sounds like a colour, but it is the sense of new to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is an idiom for someone naive or lacking practice, a novice.

clue.text: Debussy maybe receiving praise in church

indicators.note: something receiving another takes it inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A composer's music is lauded during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was the French composer, so his first name is an example signalled by 'maybe'.

clue.text: Yellow egg to lift across log for bird expert

indicators.note: one word stretched across another spans it, holding it in its middle

blocks.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
a nit is a louse egg
to hoist is to lift
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for raising a yellow egg over a fallen log, oddly attributed to a birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The log sits inside the lifting word, split after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornithologist is a scientist who studies birds.

clue.text: Possesses note that's made by one in a hurry?

definitions.text: that's made by one in a hurry

blocks.note: has means possesses
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A rushed person scribbles a quick note.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'make haste': it is what someone in a hurry makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'make haste' means hurry, so speed is the thing a rushing person makes.

clue.text: Veterans putting on plays?

blocks.note: first meaning: old hands
second meaning: people who stage theatrical productions

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is a made-up literal reading of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is an experienced person, while a stager literally stages shows.

clue.text: The inclination (but evidently not the ability)

blocks.note: first meaning: a slope or tilt
second meaning: the contraction of cannot

explanation.surface: Someone has the will to do something but plainly lacks the skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' suggests a wish, but here it is a slant; adding an apostrophe gives the word for being unable.
explanation.definitionFit: A cant is a sloping surface or tilt, and can't expresses being unable.

clue.text: Not all regular guests bicker

indicators.note: not all of the words is used, only a stretch running across them

blocks.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Some of the habitual visitors squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to quarrel over petty things, a close synonym.

clue.text: Memory loss in a very big area worried men

indicators.note: worried words are agitated, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
one thing in another sits inside it, so the shuffled piece goes within the area

blocks.note: Asia is the largest continent
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Anxious men across a vast region can no longer remember things.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged men go between the first letter of the continent and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for a partial or total loss of recall.

clue.text: Unable to escape, resident finally knocked

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
rapped means knocked

explanation.surface: A locked-in resident eventually bangs on the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Being trapped means being caught or confined with no way out.

clue.text: Subject of article by yours truly

blocks.note: the definite article
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: A writer explains what a piece they wrote is about.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or main idea of a work.

clue.text: Tailed zebras every so often, arriving at trees

indicators.note: every so often means at regular gaps, so only alternating letters are kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of each word

explanation.surface: Someone followed zebras now and then until they reached a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailed' reads as having tails, but it is the verb meaning followed.
explanation.definitionFit: Alders are a genus of trees of the birch family, often found near water.

clue.text: HF again used for broadcast from Kabul?

indicators.note: seed broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a fresh order

blocks.note: all seven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: High frequency radio is once more used to transmit from Afghanistan's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: HF really is radio jargon for high frequency, which makes 'broadcast' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabul is the capital of Afghanistan, and Afghani is an adjective for things of that country.

clue.text: Sounds and smells overwhelming one

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one part swallows the other

blocks.note: to nose is to smell or sniff out
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is swamped by a barrage of sounds and smells.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises are sounds, especially loud or unwanted ones.

clue.text: Unusual, small gym class US agents left

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
PE is physical education
the CIA is America's intelligence agency
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Something odd: American spies quit a small fitness class.
explanation.definitionFit: Special means out of the ordinary, exceptional.

clue.text: Like seabird at back of ship

blocks.note: as means like
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A gull-like bird perched at the rear of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for at or towards the rear of a boat.

clue.text: Ogre's ruined spiny shrub

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: all five letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A monster's prickly bush has been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse, also called furze, is a prickly yellow-flowered heathland plant.

clue.text: Port to consume at ten to one for example

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
taken as written

explanation.surface: Odds on drinking port at ten to one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten to one' looks like betting odds or a clock time, but it is an example of a proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten to one expresses one quantity against another, which is an example of a proportion.

clue.text: Without delay: therefore one's ahead of time

indicators.note: being ahead of something puts it first, so this part comes before the next

blocks.note: so means therefore
taken as written without the apostrophe
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone early concludes they are ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Soonest, as in 'the sooner the better', means at the earliest possible moment.

clue.text: Sailor at end of cavern finding mountain lake

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the one kept here

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sailor emerges from a cave to discover a lake in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small upland lake, a word common in northern England.

clue.text: Diplomatic staffer to fix date at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to attach is to fix
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An embassy official finally settles a date.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a specialist member of an ambassador's staff.

clue.text: Increasingly distant, keeping company no longer with queen

blocks.note: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British firm that no longer exists
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone grows more aloof, no longer keeping company with royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was a giant British chemicals company taken over in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy is used figuratively for cold and unfriendly, so icier means growing more aloof.

clue.text: Exceptionally, monsieur abandons minor row at cathedral city

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: M is the French abbreviation for monsieur
taken as written
a din is a row or racket
taken as written
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A Frenchman walks out of a small quarrel in a cathedral city, surprisingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinately means excessively or to an unusual degree.
